hints.title: Single Use Character Inventory
hints.text: Each letter in the source text can be cut out and used at most once. How can inventory tracking verify whether every required letter exists in sufficient quantity?

hints.title: Alphabet Count Deficit Early Exit
hints.text: Count the available letters across the magazine first. Then decrement the counts as each letter in the note is inspected. Any deficit proves the note impossible.

hints.title: Inventory Decrement Verification Procedure
hints.text: Record the frequency of every character in the magazine using a fixed array or map. Traverse the ransom note character by character, decrementing the corresponding frequency. If any count drops below zero or is missing, return false. If all letters are matched, return true.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(M + N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching and removing each character from the magazine string directly causes O(M * N) string manipulation overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting characters in a 26-element array takes O(M + N) time and constant O(1) space because the alphabet size is fixed.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should quickly implement the array or counter approach and mention early termination when note length exceeds magazine length.
